issue.title: Remove the pinned legacy_dependency_children key from task-status-hooks JSON after one release
issue.description:
## Feature proposal

Remove the `legacy_dependency_children` key from `bob task-status-hooks -f json` output
(and any summary-line count) once one release has shipped with it pinned at `0`.

Background: batch-14 phase bob-cli-an.6.6.6.5.6.5.5.6.6.6.6.6.6.4 (bob-cli 0f76d558)
retired the R8 legacy-child readers. The epic's `legacy_key = pin` decision kept the key
as a constant `0` for one release so log readers keep a stable hooks JSON contract, and
said a follow-up task removes it. `docs/task-dependencies.md` §10 ("Compatibility
output") and `docs/task-status-hooks.md` describe the pin.

Scope:
- Delete the key from the hooks JSON model/output (`src/native/task_status_hooks/model.rs`,
  `output.rs`) and any summary text that still mentions legacy children.
- Update `docs/task-status-hooks.md` and `docs/task-dependencies.md` §10, plus CLI tests
  that assert the key.
- This is a breaking CLI/JSON contract change: mark the commit with `!` per the release
  train decision.

Gate: actionable only after a release tag contains 0f76d558
(`git tag --contains 0f76d558`). At filing time the latest tag was v0.3.1, which does not.

Landing verification on 2026-10-26: `bob task-status-hooks --dry-run -f json` on athena
(built from master) reported `legacy_dependency_children: 0`.

Out of scope for batch 14 because its decision deliberately pinned the key for one
release instead of removing it.
